primary_topics: Short essay on equality before God, June 27, 2009 -- using CJP's own experience as Special Minister of Holy Communion as the governing illustration

The Fr. Antonio Rosales conversation: when CJP became Chief Justice, his parish priest offered special arrangements; CJP replied: 'in Santuario de San Antonio, I was just an ordinary parishioner' -- no special arrangements, no extra protocol

Matthew 25 as the governing standard: God will not ask about bank account digits, doctoral degrees, or government positions; only whether we shared resources, used talent to defend the weak, and spent time to help those in need

The principle: 'in serving our Lord and our Church, we, the people of God, are all equal. Our status or wealth or education is not at all important. What is important is our desire to serve and the quality and sincerity of our service.'
sub_topics: 20-year Special Minister tenure: became one in 1989; continued after SC appointment (1995); continued after becoming Chief Justice

Fr. Rosales conversation: asked if CJP would still want to continue and what special arrangements (like security, seating protocol) he would need; CJP: 'I may be the highest judicial official of our country, but in Santuario de San Antonio, I was just an ordinary parishioner. And, if he would permit me, I would like to continue serving as a Special Minister of Holy Communion without any extra arrangements or protocols. I added that I would see to it that my security personnel who accompanied me while I was serving would be as inconspicuous as possible.'

Theological grounding: 'in serving our Lord and our Church, we, the people of God, are all equal. Our status or wealth or education is not at all important. What is important is our desire to serve and the quality and sincerity of our service.'

Matthew 25 as the final accounting standard: 'when we finally knock at the pearly gates, our Lord will not ask us how many digits were in our bank accounts, or how many doctoral degrees we earned, or how lofty our government positions were. He will just ask whether we shared our resources with the poor, used our talent to defend the weak, and spent our time to help those in most need. And if I may add, how sincerely and humbly we served the Lord and His Church on earth.'

stances.claim: The highest judicial officer of the Philippines -- when serving as Special Minister of Holy Communion -- is 'just an ordinary parishioner.' This is not false humility but the governing theological principle: in God's service, civil rank is irrelevant. CJP's refusal of special protocol is the most concrete institutional embodiment of this principle in his life.

one_paragraph_summary: Published June 27, 2009, this short essay by CJP on equality before God uses his own 20-year experience as Special Minister of Holy Communion at Santuario de San Antonio parish as the governing illustration. When he became Chief Justice, his parish priest Fr. Antonio Rosales asked if he would still want to continue and what special arrangements (security, seating protocol) he would need. CJP replied: 'I may be the highest judicial official of our country, but in Santuario de San Antonio, I was just an ordinary parishioner. And, if he would permit me, I would like to continue serving as a Special Minister of Holy Communion without any extra arrangements or protocols. I would see to it that my security personnel would be as inconspicuous as possible.' The governing principle: 'in serving our Lord and our Church, we, the people of God, are all equal. Our status or wealth or education is not at all important. What is important is our desire to serve and the quality and sincerity of our service.' He grounds this in Matthew 25: 'when we finally knock at the pearly gates, our Lord will not ask us how many digits were in our bank accounts, or how many doctoral degrees we earned, or how lofty our government positions were. He will just ask whether we shared our resources with the poor, used our talent to defend the weak, and spent our time to help those in most need. And if I may add, how sincerely and humbly we served the Lord and His Church on earth.'
